notes.title: -는 바람에
notes.text: -는 바람에 explains an unexpected cause, usually with a bad result: 늦잠을 자는 바람에 지각했어요 (I overslept, so I was late). It's an excuse-maker's best friend! 잘못 means "mistake, fault": 제 잘못이에요 (It's my fault).

notes.title: Lost and found
notes.text: Lost things in Korea often find their way home — people hand them to the 파출소 (neighborhood police box) or the subway's lost-and-found center (유실물 센터). To report something is 신고하다. 도둑 = thief, 강도 = robber, 도둑맞다 = to be robbed.

notes.title: Emergencies
notes.text: In Korea, dial 112 for the police and 119 for fire and ambulance. 사고가 났어요 = there's been an accident. -아/어도 means "even if": 아무리 조심해도 (no matter how careful you are), 비가 와도 갈 거예요 (I'll go even if it rains).

notes.title: Signs
notes.text: 금연 = no smoking, 출입 금지 = no entry, 주차 금지 = no parking, 촬영 금지 = no photos. -금지 on a sign always means "prohibited." Rule adverbs: 절대로 (never ever), 함부로 (carelessly, without asking), 마음대로 (however you please).

lessons.goal: Talk about laws, luck and things working out.

notes.title: 잘됐다!
notes.text: Korea is known for returning lost wallets and phones. 잘됐다! (That worked out! / Good for you!) is one of the most useful reactions to good news. 맞다 has several meanings: to be right (맞아요), to welcome (손님을 맞다), and to be hit (매를 맞다).
